title: Make the price check hear from every supplier

blocks.text: Purchasing compares prices before every order: `QuoteBoard.cheapest(...)` asks each supplier's API for a quote and picks the lowest. Each API can take a few seconds, so the suppliers are asked at the same time, each on a thread of its own. A supplier that doesn't stock the item answers `null` and is left out.

Last quarter a buyer ordered 600 brackets at the "cheapest" price, and it turned out that the supplier with the lowest price had been failing for a week: its answers never reached the comparison, and nothing in the logs said why.
`cheapest(...)` already compares the offers. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/QuoteBoard.java`:

items: `ask(...)`: start asking one supplier and return at once with something to collect the answer from later;

blocks.text: When you're done, the check still asks every supplier at the same time, each on a thread named `quote-<supplier>`, and a supplier that fails makes the whole check fail with `QuoteFailed`, whose cause is exactly what that supplier threw. About eight lines in total.
The tests use suppliers that answer at once, fail, or wait for one another.

cases.says: every supplier is asked, one that doesn't stock the item is left out, and the cheapest offer is returned
a supplier's failure reaches the caller with the supplier's own exception as the cause, not a wrapper around it
a supplier that fails fails the check rather than being treated as one that offers nothing
asking a supplier returns before its answer arrives, so all suppliers are asked at the same time
each supplier is asked on a thread whose name says which supplier it is

origin.section: A Runnable Has No Way Back: Return a Result or a Failure Through a Callable

concepts: A Callable wrapped in a FutureTask and run on a thread hands its result, or its failure as the cause of an ExecutionException, to whoever calls get().
